title: Learning What to Share and What to Personalize: Hierarchical Strategy Co-Evolution for Agent Memory

visual_explainer.blocker: A paper-specific mechanism figure has not yet passed grounded VISUAL_POLICY.md review; the verified bilingual deep note carries the mechanism, controls, and lifecycle caveats meanwhile.

analysis.tldr: HiPS makes memory-management policy itself hierarchical state—a shared rule layer plus persona-specific deltas—and its strongest evidence is not the heterogeneous leaderboard but ablations and cross-model transfer showing that rule flow/gating materially changes OOD personalized behavior.
analysis.problem: Static one-size-fits-all memory writers must decide what to retain, compress, or discard for users whose preferences and interaction patterns diverge; optimizing one global memory policy can erase useful shared structure or overfit persona-specific exceptions.
analysis.core_idea: Distill a Universal Strategy from cross-persona trajectories, create Persona Delta rules only when persona-specific predictive gain warrants them, and move rules between shared and personal tiers through Cross-Level Rule Flow; inject a budgeted subset of management rules while policy training and memory strategy co-evolve from outcome evidence.

memory_design.write: Universal Strategy Distillation extracts shared management rules from cross-persona outcomes; Persona Delta Distillation adds user-specific management rules only for divergent personas rather than storing every observed fact as a policy exception.
memory_design.organize: Memory-management policy is decomposed into a global shared rule set plus persona-local deltas, with evidence levels and cross-level promotion/demotion controlling where a rule belongs.
memory_design.read: At each step a budgeted submodular selector injects the relevant shared and persona-specific management rules that govern what profile evidence is retained or transformed.
memory_design.update_forget: Cross-Level Rule Flow promotes recurring personal rules to the universal tier and specializes contradicted global rules back toward persona-local state; the paper evolves policy rules, not a fully specified privacy/deletion lifecycle for underlying user facts.

compared_to: Static/global memory-management strategies and published memory baselines
Ablations without Cross-Level Rule Flow, persona gating, Universal Strategy Distillation, persona grouping, or Persona Delta Distillation
Universal-only strategy versus universal-plus-persona-delta transfer to different foundation models without policy RL
analysis.evidence: On PersonaMem, full HiPS reports 73.49/62.01 versus 64.45/55.37 for MemSkill, but baseline backbones are not fully matched. More diagnostic ablations show full PERMA scores 66.95/56.56/63.83/56.30 versus 45.39/40.87/43.12/36.50 without Cross-Level Rule Flow and 51.63/44.99/52.62/46.79 without persona gating. Learned universal+delta rules also transfer across Qwen, GPT-4o-mini, Gemini 2.5 Flash, and GPT-5 without carrying the original RL policy, supporting an external policy-state effect rather than only parameter training.
analysis.why_it_matters: Memory evolution is not only about adding/removing memories: the policy that decides what becomes memory can itself need shared and personalized state. HiPS suggests the highest-leverage boundary may be deciding which memory-management rules should generalize and which should remain user-local.
limitations: The headline cross-system table mixes different model backbones/checkpoints for some baselines, so it is not a clean component-level superiority test.
The full package jointly changes strategy distillation, persona gating, rule flow, rule selection, and policy optimization; causal credit belongs to the matched ablations rather than the total gain.
Reported evolution time grows from roughly 140 seconds at 4K dialogue context to roughly 1,700 seconds at 128K, while full dollar/energy and continual maintenance costs are not reported.
Experiments are English-centric and do not establish years-long preference drift, privacy deletion, or adversarial persona-update behavior.
